monthly_review.summary: This month shows a deliberate shift toward lower-intensity, higher-volume aerobic base building — evidenced by increased Z1 time, reduced average HR, and slightly slower pace — while maintaining VO2 max and efficiency.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 1 time jumped from 23% to 39% while Zone 4+ dropped from 19% to 1%, signaling a strategic aerobic rebuild — the most notable shift in training intent.

goal_tracker.message: You need 0.2 more km across 1 session to match last month’s distance — e.g., extend your next easy run by 200m at ~9:00–9:40 min/km pace.

insights.title: Slight efficiency dip despite stable VO2 max
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency declined from 13.66 to 13.39 m/beat this month, even though VO2 max remains steady at 37.0 — suggesting reduced cardiac output per stride or subtle form inefficiency under lower-HR conditions.

insights.title: Strong Z1/Z2 dominance with near-elimination of threshold work
insights.body: Z1+Z2 now comprise 83% of effort (vs 55% last month), while Z4+Z5 dropped from 19% to 1% — a purposeful reduction in high-intensity stress, but may delay lactate threshold adaptation if sustained >3 weeks.

insights.title: Cadence improved (+3 spm) but vertical oscillation rose slightly
insights.body: Avg cadence increased from 142 to 145 spm, yet vertical oscillation trended up (7.5–8.1 cm across recent runs vs prior month’s implied ~7.3 cm), indicating possible overstriding compensation during faster efforts like the 7:45/km run on 5/16.

insights.title: Aerobic TE dropped despite higher volume consistency
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE fell from 3.1 to 2.7 — likely due to lower average HR (135 vs 142 bpm) and slower pace — confirming this month prioritized recovery and endurance over stimulus intensity.

recommendations.action: Do a 5km Zone 2 run tomorrow (HR 130–138 bpm) with cadence consciously held at 148–150 spm and vertical oscillation target ≤7.6 cm (use real-time Garmin metrics)
recommendations.reason: Reinforces aerobic efficiency gains while stabilizing form — recent runs show cadence improves at lower HR, but vertical oscillation spikes above 7.8 cm when pace drops below 8:00/km or HR rises above 145 bpm.

recommendations.action: Insert one 8-minute Zone 3 interval (HR 148–155 bpm, pace ~7:30–7:50/km) in your next midweek run, preceded by 15 min Z2 warm-up and followed by 10 min Z1 cooldown
recommendations.reason: Last month included 26% Z3 time and 4% Z5 — reintroducing modest threshold stimulus prevents detraining while staying within safe weekly load (current avg TE is 2.7 vs last month’s 3.1).

recommendations.action: After your longest run this month (9.5 km), perform 4 × 1-min strides at 5:00/km pace with full Z1 recovery — focus on minimizing ground contact time (<305 ms) and landing under center of mass
recommendations.reason: Your fastest recent run (7:45/km on 5/16) showed elevated vertical oscillation (8.1 cm) and longer ground contact (286 ms); strides reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without adding fatigue.

weekly_focus.description: Balance foundational aerobic development with targeted neuromuscular cues to protect efficiency gains while preventing compensatory form drift during low-HR running.
